_comment: Offline port knowledge base. risk: 0-100 base risk when the port is exposed on a non-loopback interface. action: close | restrict | review | keep

20.why: FTP sends credentials and data in clear text.

21.why: FTP sends credentials in clear text and is a frequent brute-force target. Use SFTP instead.

22.why: Remote shell access. Keep only if you need it; restrict to key-based auth and trusted IPs.

23.why: Unencrypted remote shell. Should never be exposed.

25.why: Mail relay. A workstation rarely needs to accept mail; open relays are abused for spam.

53.why: DNS server. If not intentional, may be abused for amplification attacks.

67.why: Rogue DHCP servers can redirect network traffic.

80.why: Web server without encryption. Fine for local dev, risky if exposed to the network.

135.why: Windows RPC endpoint mapper; used for lateral movement. Should not be reachable from untrusted networks.

137.why: Legacy NetBIOS leaks host info and enables poisoning attacks.

139.why: Legacy SMB over NetBIOS; frequent ransomware entry point.

161.why: SNMP v1/v2 uses guessable community strings and leaks system info.

443.why: Encrypted web server. Check that it is intentional.

445.why: File sharing. Exploited by WannaCry/EternalBlue; never expose beyond trusted LAN.

554.why: Streaming server; often from cameras or media apps.

631.why: Printing service; CUPS had critical RCE bugs (CVE-2024-47176).

1080.why: Open proxies are abused to relay malicious traffic.

1433.why: Database should never be exposed to untrusted networks.

1900.why: UPnP can open router ports automatically and is used in DDoS amplification.

2049.why: Network file system; weak auth by default.

2375.why: Unauthenticated Docker API = full root access to the host.

3306.why: Database should listen on localhost only.

3389.why: Remote Desktop is the #1 ransomware entry point. Disable or put behind VPN with NLA.

4444.why: Default port of Metasploit reverse shells; highly suspicious.

5000.why: On macOS this is usually AirPlay Receiver.

5432.why: Database should listen on localhost only.

5555.why: ADB over network gives full device control.

5900.why: Remote screen control; weak passwords are common.

5985.why: Remote PowerShell; used for lateral movement.

6379.why: Redis has no auth by default; exposed instances are hijacked for cryptomining.

6667.why: IRC is a classic botnet command-and-control channel.

8888.why: Jupyter notebooks allow arbitrary code execution.

11211.why: Used in massive DDoS amplification attacks.

27017.why: Exposed MongoDB instances are routinely wiped and ransomed.
